discovery: Discovery of exoplanet transits and development of transit photometry into the method that revealed the size, composition and abundance of planets beyond the Solar System
motivation: In 1999 Charbonneau and Henry independently observed the first transit of an exoplanet, HD 209458b. This confirmed that the radial-velocity planets were real gas giants and gave the first direct measurement of a planet's radius, and so its density. Transit photometry also opened a new field of transmission and emission spectroscopy: Charbonneau and collaborators made the first detection of an exoplanet atmosphere in 2002. For decades Borucki argued, against wide scepticism, that space photometry could reach the precision needed to find Earth-sized planets. As Principal Investigator of Kepler he proved it, and found thousands of planets. Kepler showed that small planets are common and gave the first statistical census of planetary systems, including planets in habitable zones. Together these achievements turned exoplanets from a handful of Doppler signals into a precise physical science. They underpin CoRoT, TESS, CHEOPS, PLATO and JWST, and the search for life elsewhere.
